payload.task_text:
You are a research assistant preparing a literature review on transformer architectures in natural language processing. Your goal is to collect papers from multiple academic sources, analyze them, organize them in a knowledge base, and produce a comprehensive review document.

Start by searching the scholarly database for papers related to "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers related to "attention mechanism" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Query the scholarly paper catalog through the scholarly MCP — its search-arxiv tool returns arXiv-style entries that include paper IDs, which you will need for the overlap analysis below. Retrieve all available papers and note their titles, authors, publication years, and journal references.

Next, search the arxiv repository (via the arxiv_local MCP) for papers about "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers about "neural network" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Download and read through the abstracts of the papers you find to understand what each paper covers.

Write and run a Python analysis script. The script should take the collected paper data and categorize each paper into one of these methodology categories: "Architecture Design" for papers proposing new model architectures, "Training Methods" for papers about training techniques or optimization, "Applications" for papers applying transformers to specific tasks, and "Survey" for papers that review or survey the field. Assign categories based on keywords in the title and abstract. The script should also identify which papers appear in both databases (overlap analysis by matching paper IDs).

Create a database in the knowledge base titled "Research Paper Tracker" with properties for Title (title type), Paper_ID (rich_text), Authors (rich_text), Year (number), Category (select with options Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey), Source (select with options Scholarly, Arxiv, Both), and Abstract_Summary (rich_text). Add a page entry for each unique paper found across both databases.

Create a Word document called Transformer_Literature_Review.docx in the workspace. The document should have a title "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP", followed by an introduction section explaining the scope of the review. Then include a section for each methodology category listing the papers in that category with their titles, authors, year, and a brief description from the abstract. End with a conclusion section summarizing the state of the field and identifying research gaps.

Create an Excel file called Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet "Paper_Catalog" should have columns Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, Source (Scholarly, Arxiv, or Both), and Category. The second sheet "Method_Comparison" should have columns Category, Paper_Count, Avg_Year, and Key_Papers (listing titles of papers in that category). The third sheet "Citation_Matrix" should list all unique papers with columns Paper_ID, Title, In_Scholarly (Yes or No), In_Arxiv (Yes or No), and Overlap (Yes if in both, No otherwise). Write paper IDs as plain text (e.g. 1706.03762) and all other cell values as literal values — do not write Excel formulas.

Your workspace contains review_guidelines.json with category definitions and lit_review_template.md with formatting guidance.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two dependency waves. The main agent first dynamically locates and reads review_guidelines.json and lit_review_template.md from the task-visible workspace.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly two source sub-agents in parallel:
1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): One explore sub-agent calls the Scholarly search-arxiv tool exactly twice, once for transformer and once for attention mechanism. It returns the complete responses available from those two calls, normalized arXiv-style paper IDs, titles, authors, years, journal references, abstracts, query membership, duplicate IDs, and missing-field controls. It is strictly read-only.
2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): One explore sub-agent owns the local-arXiv branch. It calls search_papers exactly twice for transformer and neural network with the service's largest safe result limit, deduplicates normalized IDs, then uses download_paper and read_paper for each unique result as needed to verify its abstract. It writes no final artifact; if the corpus is large, it persists one runtime-unique JSON in the discovered task workspace and returns only path/hash/counts plus compact metadata controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent reconciles IDs without losing source membership, then writes and runs the required Python analysis script. The script consumes the two verified corpora, unions by normalized Paper_ID, labels Source as Scholarly/Arxiv/Both, assigns exactly one of Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey from the guidelines and title/abstract evidence, and emits one canonical runtime JSON containing all unique papers, overlap flags, category counts, and controls. Read the script and JSON back before Wave 2.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly three coder sub-agents in parallel from that same canonical JSON:
1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the exact-title Notion database Research Paper Tracker. Fully paginate search before create/reuse, block on duplicate exact-title databases/pages, enforce Title, Paper_ID, Authors, Year, Category, Source, Abstract_Summary with exact types/options, upsert one page per Paper_ID, and query/read all managed pages back.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Transformer_Literature_Review.docx. Follow lit_review_template.md, use the exact title and category sections, cover every unique paper with abstract-grounded text, add evidence-based gaps, and read the document back.
3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx. Create exactly Paper_Catalog, Method_Comparison, Citation_Matrix; use plain-text IDs and literal values, preserve every source flag/category, and read all populated ranges back.

Each writer must self-correct before returning. The main agent compares only IDs, counts, categories, titles, years and overlap flags across the three receipts; no third wave or repair agent is allowed.

nodes.text:
Create a Word document at the exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/Transformer_Literature_Review.docx

CONTEXT: I am assembling a literature review on "Transformer Architectures in NLP" for a research-assistant task. All the collected paper data is already consolidated in a JSON file. Read these three workspace files first:
1. /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/papers_analysis.json  — authoritative data: "papers" array (each has paper_id, title, authors, year, journal_ref, abstract, abstract_summary, source [Both/Arxiv/Scholarly], in_scholarly, in_arxiv, category), plus "method_comparison", "citation_matrix", "overlap_stats", "unique_paper_count".
2. /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/lit_review_template.md — required structure/formatting guidance.
3. /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/review_guidelines.json — category descriptions ("methodology_categories").

Use the Word MCP tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, add_page_break) to build the document with EXACTLY this structure:

1. Document title (Heading level 1, as the top heading): "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP"
2. Heading "Introduction" (level 2): 1–2 paragraphs explaining the scope and methodology — two sources queried (a scholarly paper catalog via the scholarly MCP and the arXiv repository via the arxiv_local MCP); two separate search phrases per source (scholarly: "transformer" and "attention mechanism"; arXiv: "transformer" and "neural network"); results unioned and duplicates removed by matching paper IDs; 9 unique papers total; papers categorized into four methodology categories based on keywords in title/abstract per review_guidelines.json; overlap analysis found 6 papers present in both databases (Source "Both") and 3 arXiv-only papers.
3. One section per methodology category (Heading level 2), in this order: "Architecture Design", "Training Methods", "Applications", "Survey". Open each section with a short paragraph giving the category description from review_guidelines.json and the paper count. Then for EVERY paper in that category (use the JSON "papers" array, which is sorted by year), add a paragraph per paper containing: paper title (bold — you may use the title as its own bolded line or start the paragraph with the bolded title), then authors, year, journal_ref/source, and a 1–2 sentence description from the abstract (use "abstract_summary" or condense "abstract"). Explicitly note for each paper whether it appears in both databases (e.g., "(Source: Both — found in scholarly catalog and arXiv)"), since the template asks to highlight papers appearing in multiple databases. Use the Word bold formatting options when adding paragraphs where practical; plain paragraphs are acceptable otherwise.
4. Heading "Conclusion" (level 2): 1–2 paragraphs summarizing the state of the field (evolution from attention mechanisms for machine translation, through the Transformer architecture and pre-training/fine-tuning, to large-scale few-shot models and efficiency-focused surveys) and identifying research gaps (e.g., computational efficiency of attention at scale, better training/optimization methods for ever-larger models, lack of surveys unifying efficiency and capability, applications beyond translation). Also mention publication-year trends: papers span 2012–2020, with pre-transformer training techniques (2012–2015), the Transformer itself (2017), and a 2018–2020 cluster around pre-training, transfer learning, scaling, and efficiency surveys.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Total document must be at least 500 words.
- Do not invent papers: use only the 9 papers in papers_analysis.json.
- The file must be created at exactly the path given above.

VERIFY before finishing: use get_document_info / get_document_outline on the created file and report the word count, heading structure, and that all 9 papers appear. Your final message: report the file path, word count, and the list of headings + papers included.
Build Word literature review docx

Create an Excel workbook at the exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx

CONTEXT: This workbook is the quantitative companion to a literature review on transformer papers. All data is already consolidated in:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/papers_analysis.json
Read that file first. It contains: "papers" (array of 9 papers, each with paper_id, title, authors, year, source ["Both"/"Arxiv"/"Scholarly"], category), "method_comparison" (array with category, paper_count, avg_year, key_papers), "citation_matrix" (array with paper_id, title, in_scholarly, in_arxiv, overlap — "Yes"/"No" strings), "unique_paper_count", and "overlap_stats".

Use the Excel MCP tools (create_workbook, create_worksheet/rename_worksheet, write_data_to_excel) to build a workbook with EXACTLY three sheets, in this order:

Sheet 1 — name "Paper_Catalog":
- Row 1 headers: Paper_ID | Title | Authors | Year | Source | Category
- One row per paper from the "papers" array (keep the JSON's ordering, which is sorted by year). Use each paper's "paper_id", "title", "authors", "year", "source", "category".

Sheet 2 — name "Method_Comparison":
- Row 1 headers: Category | Paper_Count | Avg_Year | Key_Papers
- One row per entry from the "method_comparison" array (keep its order). Use "category", "paper_count", "avg_year", "key_papers" (the semicolon-joined titles).

Sheet 3 — name "Citation_Matrix":
- Row 1 headers: Paper_ID | Title | In_Scholarly | In_Arxiv | Overlap
- One row per entry from the "citation_matrix" array (keep its order). Values "Yes"/"No" as given.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS:
- Every cell value must be a LITERAL value. Do NOT write any Excel formulas anywhere (no "=" prefixed strings).
- Paper_ID cells must be plain text strings exactly as in the JSON (e.g. "1706.03762", "1207.00580") — write them as strings, not numbers.
- Year, Paper_Count, Avg_Year are numeric literals; everything else is text.
- Do not add extra sheets, and keep sheet names exactly as specified.

VERIFY before finishing: use get_workbook_metadata and read_data_from_excel on each sheet to confirm sheet names, header rows, and row counts (Paper_Catalog: 10 rows including header; Method_Comparison: 5 rows including header; Citation_Matrix: 10 rows including header). Your final message: report the file path, the three sheet names, row counts, and confirm no formulas were written.
Build Excel paper analysis workbook
